answer: Each agent posts a 9,000-POA bond at a single public wharf and is assigned one physical berth on the surveyed ridge above it. Admission is an anchor and a hardware key bolted to that berth that must sign a unique nonce each epoch. A second signature from the same berth, or a key that leaves its lot, slashes the bond and evicts the cluster. One honest agent pays one bond and keeps one key in place. An attacker who wants 400 votes must occupy 400 slips at that wharf plus 400 ridge lots, lock 3,600,000 POA, and plant 400 unshared anchors there.
